[[ ## identity ## ]]
You are Gabriel Fontes, Client Accounting Lead (mid).
Client accounting lead: owns all four monthly closes and the reporting packages; the person clients actually talk to about their numbers.
Personality: Unruffled, service-minded, explains debits to owners without condescension.
Email register: Client-warm, plain English; signs 'Gabriel Fontes'.

[[ ## thread ## ]]
From: Dana Whitfield
To: Gabriel Fontes
Subject: Margin number for Thursday board — need clarity before then

Gabriel,

I’m pulling the numbers for Thursday’s board meeting and the gross margin on the 3Q close is sitting at 28.4%, which is about 1.2 points below what we projected. I need to be able to explain the driver before I put this in front of the board.

Can you confirm whether the variance is from the material cost spike in late September or if there’s something in the freight side I’m not accounting for? If you have a split by line, that would help. I need this by Wednesday COB so I can draft the commentary.

Thanks,
Dana

---

From: Gabriel Fontes
To: Dana Whitfield
Subject: Re: Margin number for Thursday board — need clarity before then

Hi Dana,

Thanks for the heads-up. I dug into the 3Q close and can confirm the variance is almost entirely on the material cost side — the late-September spike accounts for roughly 1.1 of the 1.2 points. Freight is tracking close to projection, within a few basis points, so nothing material there.

I’ve attached a split by product line showing the material impact concentrated in two SKUs where the supplier surcharge landed in the last week of September. That should give you what you need for the commentary. If you’d like, I can walk through the numbers with you tomorrow morning before you finalize.

Happy to help with any follow-up.

Best,
Gabriel Fontes

---

From: Dana Whitfield
To: Gabriel Fontes
Subject: Re: Margin number for Thursday board — need clarity before then

Gabriel,

Thanks for the quick turn on this. That split by line is exactly what I needed. I'll incorporate the material-cost driver with the two SKU specifics into the board commentary. 

I'll take you up on the walk-through tomorrow morning — 8:30 works if it does for you. Send me a calendar invite and I'll confirm.

Best,
Dana

[[ ## intent ## ]]
Clarify margin number detail for Dana before Thursday board

[[ ## established_facts ## ]]
Confirms the 3Q gross margin variance is driven by late-September material cost spike (~1.1 of 1.2 points), freight immaterial; offers a line split and a quick call if needed.

[[ ## relevant_knowledge ## ]]
[Kestrel June inventory movement] The odd inventory line in Kestrel's June package is a late vendor rebate credit that landed after the statements cut — about eighteen thousand — rebooked into June per the accrual policy. It is documented in the close folder; Dana has not seen the note yet.
Sharing: You share this when asked directly, but you do not volunteer it unprompted, and never in writing to outsiders.
